n_last)\n    keep = causal | (~in_last_block)\n    scale = 1.0 / math.sqrt(D)\n    scores = torch.matmul(q2.float(), k.float().transpose(-1, -2)) * scale\n    scores = scores.masked_fill(~keep[None, None, :, :], float(\"-inf\"))\n    probs = F.softmax(scores, dim=-1)\n    out = torch.matmul(probs, v.float())\n    return out.to(q2.dtype)\n\n\ndef cos_sim(a, b):\n    a, b = a.float().flatten(), b.float().flatten()\n    return (a @ b) / (a.norm() * b.norm() + 1e-12)\n\n\ndef test_a_shape(B=1, H=4, qN=2048, kN=2048, D=128, n_init=8, n_local=512):\n    print(f\"\\n--- test_a_shape B={B} H={H} qN={qN} kN={kN} D={D} n_init={n_init} n_local={n_local} ---\")\n    torch.manual_seed(0)\n    q = torch.randn(B, H, qN, D, device=\"cuda\", dtype=torch.bfloat16) * 0.1\n    k = torch.randn(B, H, kN, D, device=\"cuda\", dtype=torch.bfloat16) * 0.1\n    v = torch.randn(B, H, kN, D, device=\"cuda\", dtype=torch.bfloat16) * 0.1\n\n    out = a_shape_attn(q, k, v, n_init=n_init, n_local=n_local)\n    ref = reference_a_shape(q, k, v, n_init=n_init, n_local=n_local)\n    cs = cos_sim(out, ref).item()\n    err = (out.float() - ref.float()).abs().max().item()\n    print(f\"  cos_sim={cs:.6f}  max_abs_err={err:.4e}\")\n    assert cs > 0.99, f\"cos_sim {cs} below 0.99\"\n    assert err < 5e-2, f\"max_abs_err {err} above 5e-2\"\n    print(\"  ✓ a_shape pass\")\n\n\ndef test_dense_last(B=1, H=4, kN=2048, D=128, n_last=128):\n    print(f\"\\n--- test_dense_last B={B} H={H} kN={kN} D={D} n_last={n_last} ---\")\n    torch.manual_seed(1)\n    k = torch.randn(B, H, kN, D, device=\"cuda\", dtype=torch.bfloat16) * 0.1\n    v = torch.randn(B, H, kN, D, device=\"cuda\", dtype=torch.bfloat16) * 0.1\n    q2 = torch.randn(B, H, n_last, D, device=\"cuda\", dtype=torch.bfloat16) * 0.1\n\n    out = dense_attn_with_last_causal(q2, k, v, n_last=n_last)\n    ref = reference_dense_with_last_causal(q2, k, v, n_last=n_last)\n    cs = cos_sim(out, ref).item()\n    err = (out.float() - ref.float()).abs().max().item()\n    print(f\"  cos_sim={cs:.6f}  max_abs_err={err:.4e}\")\n    assert cs > 0.999, f\"cos_sim {cs} below 0.999\"\n    assert err < 1e-3, f\"max_abs_err {err} above 1e-3\"\n    print(\"  ✓ dense_last pass\")\n\n\ndef test_tri_shape(B=1, H=4, N=2048, D=128, n_init=8, n_local=512, n_last=128):\n    print(f\"\\n--- test_tri_shape B={B} H={H} N={N} D={D} n_init={n_init} n_local={n_local} n_last={n_last} ---\")\n    torch.manual_seed(2)\n    q = torch.randn(B, H, N, D, device=\"cuda\", dtype=torch.bfloat16) * 0.1\n    k = torch.randn(B, H, N, D, device=\"cuda\", dtype=torch.bfloat16) * 0.1\n    v = torch.randn(B, H, N, D, device=\"cuda\", dtype=torch.bfloat16) * 0.1\n\n    out = tri_shape_attn(q, k, v, n_init=n_init, n_local=n_local, n_last=n_last)\n    # reference: concat of a_shape(q1, k1, v1) + dense_last(q2, k, v)\n    q1 = q[:, :, :-n_last]\n    q2 = q[:, :, -n_last:]\n    k1 = k[:, :, : -n_last]\n    v1 = v[:, :, : -n_last]\n    ref1 = reference_a_shape(q1, k1, v1, n_init=n_init, n_local=n_local)\n    ref2 = reference_dense_with_last_causal(q2, k, v, n_last=n_last)\n    ref = torch.cat([ref1, ref2], dim=2)\n    cs = cos_sim(out, ref).item()\n    err = (out.float() - ref.float()).abs().max().item()\n    print(f\"  cos_sim={cs:.6f}  max_abs_err={err:.4e}\")\n    assert cs > 0.99, f\"cos_sim {cs} below 0.99\"\n    assert err < 5e-2, f\"max_abs_err {err} above 5e-2\"\n    print(\"  ✓ tri_shape pass\")\n\n\ndef test_tri_shape_big(B=1, H=32, N=8192, D=128, n_init=8, n_local=512, n_last=128):\n    \"\"\"Production-shape test: H=32, longer N. Uses smaller H first to fit GPU\n    if it is shared.\"\"\"\n    print(f\"\\n--- test_tri_shape_big B={B} H={H} N={N} D={D} ---\")\n    torch.manual_seed(3)\n    q = torch.randn(B, H, N, D, device=\"cuda\", dtype=torch.bfloat16) * 0.1\n    k = torch.randn(B, H, N, D, device=\"cuda\", dtype=torch.bfloat16) * 0.1\n    v = torch.randn(B, H, N, D, device=\"cuda\", dtype=torch.bfloat16) * 0.1\n    out = tri_shape_attn(q, k, v, n_init=n_init, n_local=n_local, n_last=n_last)\n    q1 = q[:, :, :-n_last]\n    q2 = q[:, :, -n_last:]\n    ref1 = reference_a_shape(q1, k[:, :, :-n_last], v[:, :, :-n_last], n_init=n_init, n_local=n_local)\n    ref2 = reference_dense_with_last_causal(q2, k, v, n_last=n_last)\n    ref = torch.cat([ref1, ref2], dim=2)\n    cs = cos_sim(out, ref).item()\n    err = (out.float() - ref.float()).abs().max().item()\n    print(f\"  cos_sim={cs:.6f}  max_abs_err={err:.4e}\")\n    assert cs > 0.99\n    assert err < 5e-2\n    print(\"  ✓ tri_shape_big pass\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    assert torch.cuda.is_available()\n    test_a_shape()\n    test_dense_last()\n    test_tri_shape()\n    test_tri_shape_big()\n    print(\"\\n[ALL PASS]\")\n"
}

  "new_string": "def _trianglemix_probe_dump():\n    \"\"\"Snapshot the current probe state to JSON (overwriting). Cheap O(L)\n    GPU→CPU syncs. Called incrementally from the probe path so we never\n    rely on subprocess atexit (sglang scheduler runs in a worker process).\"\"\"\n    with _MINICPM_TRIANGLEMIX_PROBE_LOCK:\n        state = {}\n        for li, s in _MINICPM_TRIANGLEMIX_PROBE_STATE.items():\n            mm = s[\"middle_mass\"]\n            tm = s[\"total_mass\"]\n            if torch.is_tensor(mm):\n                mm = float(mm.detach().cpu().item())\n            if torch.is_tensor(tm):\n                tm = float(tm.detach().cpu().item())\n            state[str(li)] = {\n                \"middle_mass\": mm,\n                \"total_mass\": tm,\n                \"n_q\": int(s[\"n_q\"]),\n                \"n_k_seen\": int(s[\"n_k_seen\"]),\n                \"middle_ratio\": (mm / tm) if tm > 0 else 0.0,\n            }\n        try:\n            tmp = _MINICPM_TRIANGLEMIX_PROBE_OUTPUT + \".tmp\"\n            with open(tmp, \"w\") as f:\n                json.dump(\n                    {\n                        \"n_init\": _MINICPM_TRIANGLEMIX_PROBE_N_INIT,\n                        \"n_local\": _MINICPM_TRIANGLEMIX_PROBE_N_LOCAL,\n                        \"n_last\": _MINICPM_TRIANGLEMIX_PROBE_N_LAST,\n                        \"probe_layers\": list(_MINICPM_TRIANGLEMIX_PROBE_LAYERS),\n                        \"state\": state,\n                    },\n                    f,\n                    indent=2,\n                )\n            os.replace(tmp, _MINICPM_TRIANGLEMIX_PROBE_OUTPUT)\n        except Exception as e:\n            print(f\"[trianglemix-probe] dump failed: {e}\", flush=True)"
}

For q at row r, the matching\n       k position is `k_len - q_len + r`.\"\"\"\n    B, H, qN, D = q.shape\n    kN = k.shape[2]\n    q_pos = torch.arange(kN - qN, kN, device=q.device)  # (qN,)\n    k_pos = torch.arange(kN, device=q.device)  # (kN,)\n    diff = q_pos[:, None] - k_pos[None, :]  # (qN, kN)\n    is_window = (diff >= 0) & (diff < n_local)\n    is_sink = (k_pos[None, :] < n_init).expand(qN, kN)\n    keep = is_window | is_sink\n\n    scale = 1.0 / math.sqrt(D)\n    scores = torch.matmul(q.float(), k.float().transpose(-1, -2)) * scale\n    scores = scores.masked_fill(~keep[None, None, :, :], float(\"-inf\"))\n    probs = F.softmax(scores, dim=-1)\n    out = torch.matmul(probs, v.float())\n    return out.to(q.dtype)",
  "new_string": "def reference_a_shape(q, k, v, n_init, n_local):\n    \"\"\"fp32 reference matching MInference's a_shape kernel exactly.\n    Two-segment online softmax:\n      seg1 (sliding window): q sees k where q-k in [0, n_local).\n      seg2 (sink, complement): q sees k where k < n_init AND q-k >= n_local.\n    The union is causal (k <= q is implied by both clauses).\"\"\"\n    B, H, qN, D = q.shape\n    kN = k.shape[2]\n    q_pos = torch.arange(kN - qN, kN, device=q.device)\n    k_pos = torch.arange(kN, device=q.device)\n    diff = q_pos[:, None] - k_pos[None, :]\n    is_window = (diff >= 0) & (diff < n_local)\n    is_sink = (k_pos[None, :] < n_init) & (diff >= n_local)\n    keep = is_window | is_sink\n\n    scale = 1.0 / math.sqrt(D)\n    scores = torch.matmul(q.float(), k.float().transpose(-1, -2)) * scale\n    scores = scores.masked_fill(~keep[None, None, :, :], float(\"-inf\"))\n    probs = F.softmax(scores, dim=-1)\n    out = torch.matmul(probs, v.float())\n    return out.to(q.dtype)"

> SYSTEM

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - **Continuing from prior session**: Integrate TriangleMix (arXiv:2507.21526) attention pattern (sink + sliding window + last-N dense) into MiniCPM-SALA SGLang fork as a layer-level dispatch alongside InfLLM-v2 sparse. Goal: long-ctx prefill TTFT improvement.
   - **/goal directive (重复 2 次)**: "按照计划 永不放弃 持续工作 直到任务得到圆满和彻底完成 做好版本管理和文档记录" — Follow the plan, never give up, work to completion, do version management and documentation.
   - **User interrupt #1**: "打断一下 只在2k ctx做的么？ 可以考虑在 sglanghook 出来 这个可以支持更长上下文 选择更科学 这是我最后一次打断你" — 2K ctx too short, hook into sglang for longer ctx, more scientific selection.
   - **User interrupt #2** (critical): "不会再 sglang 中打点？ 你知道我在说什么？ 为什么不直接用 nvfp4权重 在 sglang 真实运行中收集？" — Why not instrument in sglang directly using NVFP4 weights in real sglang runs?
   - **Stop hook feedback**: Tasks not complete. P1 done (2K HF), P1.5 in progress (65K NVFP4 SGLang), P2 ported but untested, P3 dispatch written but untested, P4-P7 pending.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **TriangleMix**: training-free static attention pattern (sink n_init=8 + sliding window n_local=512 + last n_last=128 dense), O(N²) → O(N)
   - **MiniCPM-SALA hybrid architecture**: 32 layers = 8 std FA (id [0,9,16,17,22,29,30,31]) + 24 Lightning Attention (GLA)
   - **NVFP4 quantization**: production weights at `/user_4813494d/models/openbmb/MiniCPM-SALA-gptq46-calib90-90k-NVFP4-det`
   - **SGLang paged-KV**: `(num_pages, page_size=1, H_kv, D)`, access via `req_to_token[rpi, :kv_len]`
   - **Chunked prefill**: chunk-size=8192, last chunk detection via `extend_prefix_lens + extend_seq_lens == seq_lens`
   - **GQA**: H_q=32, H_kv=2, group=16
   - **Gradient probe (paper Section 2.4)**: element-wise θ multiplied into post-softmax, backward to get `|grad(aw)*aw|` in middle Q-K region
   - **Forward-mass probe**: forward-only attribution — middle_mass / total_mass per layer
   - **Triton FA-2 kernel**: TritonMultiStageDotProductionAttention.append/finalize from MInference

4. Errors and fixes:
   - **Lightning attention OOM (32 GiB allocation)**: HF passes 4D causal mask to all layers; lightning's `get_unpad_data(attention_mask[:, -q_len:])` misreads it as padding mask, creates B*Q*K indices. Fixed with forward_pre_hook setting `attention_mask=None` on 24 lightning layers (batch=1 → contiguous packed path).
   
   - **extend_seq_lens_cpu attribute error**: `'list' object has no attribute 'tolist'` — Fixed with helper:
   ```python
   def _to_list(x):
       if x is None: return None
       return x.tolist() if torch.is_tensor(x) else list(x)
   ```
   
   - **SGLang atexit didn't fire**: sglang scheduler runs in subprocess, module atexit unreliable. Fixed by calling `_trianglemix_probe_dump()` incrementally at the end of each `_forward_extend_triangle_probe`, with atomic rename via `.tmp` file.
   
   - **test_kernel cos_sim 0.91 fail**: My reference allowed `k<n_init` keep without causal check — fixed reference to match MInference's two-segment semantics:
   ```python
   is_window = (diff >= 0) & (diff < n_local)
   is_sink = (k_pos[None, :] < n_init) & (diff >= n_local)
   keep = is_window | is_sink
   ```
   
   - **P3 smoke crash**: `q2 = q[:, :, :, :]  # placeholder, will reassign` left in code, IndexError on 2D tensor. Fixed by deleting that placeholder line.

127	  - B. P1 probe 选 contribution 最低 3 个: `SGLANG_TRIANGLEMIX_LAYERS=<probe_top3>`
128	  - C. P1 probe 选 contribution 最低 6 个: `SGLANG_TRIANGLEMIX_LAYERS=<probe_top6>`
129	- 每 sample max_tokens 取自 perf_public_set 字段
130	- 跟 gold 比对，复刻 `toolkit/` 评测逻辑
131	- 输出 3×3 表（layer set × 任务类型）
132	
133	**完成判据**
134	- 30 个 sample 都跑通
135	- niah/qa 任一组 accuracy gap > 10% → 警告，但不阻塞 P5（可作为后续调 layer set 的依据）
136	- cwe gap 容忍：paper Llama 上 cwe baseline 也只有 2.2，本仓 cwe baseline 未知，先看数据
137	
138	---

140	### P5 — TTFT bench
141	
142	**目标**：量化 Triangle 在不同 ctx + layer set 下的 prefill TTFT 改进。
143	
144	**做什么**
145	- 复用 `bench/prefill_backend_compare/bench.py` 框架（max_tokens=1, 长样本截断到目标长度）
146	- 4 组配置 NO_SPEC + minicpm_flashinfer + dense_len=16K：
147	  - A. baseline: `LAYERS=""`
148	  - B. P1 probe 最低 3 个
149	  - C. P1 probe 最低 6 个
150	  - D. 全 std layer 都走 Triangle (`0,9,16,17,22,29,30,31`) — upper bound
151	- ctx ∈ {16K, 32K, 64K, 128K, 256K}
152	- repeats=3 取 min
153	
154	**完成判据**
155	- 拿到 5×4=20 cell TTFT 表
156	- 128K 上 C 配置 TTFT 下降 ≥ 25%（paper Llama 是 -32%, 我们 std layer 比例不同所以放宽）
157	- 256K 上 D 配置 TTFT 下降 ≥ 40%
158	
159	**输出**：`trianglemix/results.md` 表格 + raw json
160	
161	---

163	### P6 — EAGLE smoke
164	
165	**目标**：start_eagle.sh + Triangle 启用，server 不报错运行，长 ctx chat 出人话。
166	
167	**做什么**

169	- 启动 server
170	- 跑 mini chat：发 cwe 样本（127K tokens）+ niah 样本（127K tokens）各 1 次
171	- 跑 `bench/mini_bench.sh`，看 aggregate tok/s 不为 0（不严格要求 accept length 不退化）
172	
173	**完成判据**
174	- server 启动不报错
175	- 长 ctx chat 不乱码（出人话即可）
176	- mini_bench 跑完出数字（不论好坏）
177	
178	**不在意**
179	- mean accept length 是否退化（draft 可重训作为后续任务）
180	- aggregate tok/s 跟原 baseline 对比
181

184	### P7 — start_eagle.sh wire-in
185	
186	**目标**：把 P5 选出的最佳 Triangle 配置作为 start_eagle.sh 默认，端到端 prefill TTFT 提升。

193	  ```
194	- 跑 `toolkit/bench_serving.sh http://127.0.0.1:30000` 完整 bench
195	- 对比 commit 前后的 TTFT
196	- 更新 `docs/prefill/current.md` 记录新 baseline
197	
198	**完成判据**
199	- 端到端 bench TTFT 提升（数字 > 0 即 OK，prefill 是唯一目标）
200	- 无 runtime 报错

3	
4	方法：

34	def load_long_sample_ids():

41	    )

45	    longest = None

47	    with src.open() as fp:

49	            d = json.loads(line)
50	            if d["prompt_tokens"] > longest_pt and d["task"] == "cwe":
51	                longest_pt = d["prompt_tokens"]
52	                longest = d
53	    print(f"base sample: idx={longest['index']} task={longest['task']} prompt_tokens={longest['prompt_tokens']}")
54	
55	    ids = tok.encode(longest["question"], add_special_tokens=False)
56	    print(f"tokenized ids length: {len(ids)}")
57	
58	    # 拼接到 max(CONTEXT_LENS) + 一点 buffer
59	    target = max(CONTEXT_LENS) + 1024
60	    while len(ids) < target:
61	        ids = ids + ids
62	    print(f"after concat, ids length: {len(ids)} (target ≥ {target})")
63	    return tok, ids

66	def make_prompt_n_tokens(tok, base_ids, n_tokens):
67	    """截取/构造恰好 n_tokens 长度的 prompt text。"""
68	    truncated = base_ids[:n_tokens]
69	    text = tok.decode(truncated, skip_special_tokens=False)

73	def wait_server_ready(timeout_s=180):
74	    t0 = time.time()
75	    while time.time() - t0 < timeout_s:
76	        try:
77	            with urllib.request.urlopen(f"{API}/v1/models", timeout=2) as r:
78	                _ = r.read()
79	            return True
80	        except Exception:

84	
85	def call_completions(prompt, max_tokens=1):
86	    body = {
87	        "model": "minicpm",
88	        "prompt": prompt,
89	        "max_tokens": max_tokens,
90	        "temperature": 0.0,
91	    }

95	        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
96	    )
97	    t0 = time.time()
98	    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=TIMEOUT) as r:
99	        data = json.loads(r.read())
100	    t1 = time.time()
101	    usage = data.get("usage", {})
102	    return {
103	        "wall_s": t1 - t0,
104	        "prompt_tokens": usage.get("prompt_tokens", 0),
105	        "completion_tokens": usage.get("completion_tokens", 0),
106	    }
107	
108	
109	def main():
110	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
111	    ap.add_argument("--label", required=True, help="结果文件名 suffix，建议 'minicpm_flashinfer' 或 'flashinfer'")
112	    args = ap.parse_args()

119

122	        sys.exit(2)

125	    tok, base_ids = load_long_sample_ids()
126	
127	    results = []

130	        # 先 warmup（cold path / compile / kv 分配）
131	        for _ in range(WARMUP_PER_CTX):
132	            try:

134	            except Exception as e:
135	                print(f"  warmup {n_tok} err: {e}")
136	        walls = []

139	            try:

141	                walls.append(r["wall_s"])
142	                actual_pt = r["prompt_tokens"]
143	            except Exception as e:
144	                print(f"  err ctx={n_tok} rep={i}: {e}")
145	        if not walls:

147	            results.append({"ctx_target": n_tok, "failed": True})
148	            continue
149	        rec = {

151	            "prompt_tokens": actual_pt,

153	            "wall_med_s": statistics.median(walls),
154	            "wall_max_s": max(walls),
155	            "tok_per_s_at_min": actual_pt / min(walls) if actual_pt else None,
156	            "walls_s": walls,
157	        }
158	        results.append(rec)

161	            f"min={rec['wall_min_s']*1000:>8.1f}ms  med={rec['wall_med_s']*1000:>8.1f}ms  "
162	            f"max={rec['wall_max_s']*1000:>8.1f}ms  tok/s={rec['tok_per_s_at_min']:>8.0f}"
163	        )
164	
165	    ts = time.strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S")
166	    out_path = OUT_DIR / f"{ts}_{label}.json"
167	    out = {
168	        "label": label,
169	        "ts": ts,
170	        "context_lens": CONTEXT_LENS,
171	        "repeats": REPEATS,
172	        "results": results,
173	    }
174	    out_path.write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=2))
175	    print(f"\nsaved: {out_path}")

    echo \"[p5] server pid=${pid} died\" >&2\n            tail -50 \"${log}\" >&2\n            return 1\n        fi\n        sleep 2\n    done\n    echo \"[p5] server pid=${pid} timeout\" >&2\n    return 1\n}\n\nfor label in \"${ORDER[@]}\"; do\n    layers=\"${CONFIGS[$label]}\"\n    log=\"/tmp/p5_${label}.log\"\n    echo \"==================================================\"\n    echo \"[p5] config=${label} layers='${layers}' ctx=${CTX_LIST}\"\n    echo \"==================================================\"\n    pid=$(start_server \"${layers}\" \"${log}\")\n    echo \"[p5] server pid=${pid} log=${log}\"\n    if ! wait_ready \"${log}\" \"${pid}\"; then\n        echo \"[p5] SKIP ${label} (server not ready)\"\n        bash bench/kill_sglang.sh >/dev/null 2>&1 || true\n        continue\n    fi\n    echo \"[p5] server ready, running bench\"\n    BENCH_CTX_LIST=\"${CTX_LIST}\" python3 /user_4813494d/openbmb/bench/trianglemix/p5_bench_call.py --label \"${label}\" 2>&1 | tee -a \"/tmp/p5_${label}_bench.log\"\n    bash bench/kill_sglang.sh >/dev/null 2>&1 || true\n    sleep 3\ndone\n\necho \"[p5] all configs done; results in ${RESULTS_DIR}\"\nls -lt \"${RESULTS_DIR}\" | head -10\n\npython3 /user_4813494d/openbmb/bench/trianglemix/p5_aggregate.py\n"

# SOAR-Toolkit

<a href="README.md">中文</a> | <a href="README_EN.md">English</a>

</div>

---

本次比赛围绕 OpenBMB MiniCPM-SALA 模型的推理性能优化展开。参赛者需在指定的硬件环境上基于官方提供的 MiniCPM-SALA 模型进行优化，不得提交或替换任何基座模型。为了方便各位参赛选手进行自测，我们提供了以下评测工具，帮助大家进行检验和合理规划。主要包括：

# 基础镜像

## 镜像下载

我们提供了可运行模型并进行推理的基础镜像（内置 SGLang 及必要依赖），用于本地开发、调试与评测自测。

```bash
# 国内下载（阿里云ACR）
docker pull modelbest-registry.cn-beijing.cr.aliyuncs.com/public/soar-toolkit:latest

# 海外下载（Github）
docker pull ghcr.io/openbmb/soar-toolkit:latest
```

## MiniCPM-SALA 模型下载

### 方式一：通过 Hugging Face 下载
在下载前，请先通过如下命令安装 Hugging Face 官方 CLI 工具。
```bash
pip install huggingface_hub
```
下载完整模型库到指定路径文件夹./models
```bash
huggingface-cli download OpenBMB/MiniCPM-SALA --local-dir ./models
```

### 方式二：通过 ModelScope 下载
在下载前，请先通过如下命令安装 ModelScope。
```bash
pip install modelscope
```

207	def extract_final_answer(pred):
208	    """Extract content after </think> tag, falling back to full prediction."""
209	    parts = pred.split('</think>')
210	    return parts[-1].strip() if len(parts) > 1 else pred
211	
212	def extract_mcq_answer(pred):
213	    """Extract MCQ answer letter from prediction, supporting multiple formats."""
214	    # Format 1: ANSWER: X (standard)
215	    match = re.search(r'(?i)ANSWER\s*:\s*([A-D])', pred)
216	    if match:
217	        return match.group(1).upper()
218	    # Format 2: \boxed{\text{X}} or \boxed{X} (LaTeX)
219	    match = re.search(r'\\boxed\{\\text\{([A-D])\}\}', pred)
220	    if match:
221	        return match.group(1).upper()
222	    match = re.search(r'\\boxed\{([A-D])\}', pred)
223	    if match:
224	        return match.group(1).upper()
225	    return None
226	
227	def score_mcq(pred, gold):
228	    if not pred or not gold: return 0, None
229	    final = extract_final_answer(pred)
230	    extracted = extract_mcq_answer(final)
231	    if extracted and extracted.upper() == gold.upper():
232	        return 1, extracted
233	    return 0, extracted
234	
235	def score_exact_match(pred, gold, task="unknown"):
236	    if not pred or not gold: return 0
237	    final = extract_final_answer(pred)
238	    if not isinstance(gold, list): gold = [gold]
239	    
240	    # 针对长文本任务评分的瑕疵修复：
241	    # 如果是 QA 类型的任务，gold 列表通常是同一答案的不同表述（同义词），只要命中任意一个就算满分 1。
242	    # 如果是 CWE/FWE 类型的任务，gold 列表是必须全部提取出来的多个关键词，则算覆盖率。
243	    if task in ['qa', 'niah', 'lcx']:
244	        # 只要包含任意一个候选答案即为完全正确
245	        hits = any(str(r).lower() in final.lower() for r in gold)
246	        return 1.0 if hits else 0.0
247	    else:
248	        # cwe, fwe 等需要提取所有目标词汇的任务
249	        hits = sum([1.0 if str(r).lower() in final.lower() else 0.0 for r in gold])
250	        return hits / len(gold) if gold else 0

Configurable subset:\ndefault 5 samples each of cwe/niah/qa = 15 samples.\n\nThis script DOES NOT start/stop the server — it expects a running server on\nhttp://127.0.0.1:30000 with the desired SGLANG_TRIANGLEMIX_LAYERS env in effect.\n\"\"\"\nimport argparse\nimport json\nimport os\nimport re\nimport sys\nimport time\nimport urllib.request\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nAPI = os.environ.get(\"BENCH_API\", \"http://127.0.0.1:30000\")\nTIMEOUT = int(os.environ.get(\"BENCH_TIMEOUT\", \"1800\"))\nOUT_DIR = Path(\"/user_4813494d/openbmb/bench/trianglemix/p4_results\")\nOUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n\n# 索引段（perf_public_set 0..149，每 task 30 个）\nDEFAULT_SAMPLE_RANGES = {\n    \"cwe\": [141, 142, 143, 144, 145],\n    \"niah\": [51, 52, 53, 54, 55],\n    \"qa\": [81, 82, 83, 84, 85],\n}\n\n\ndef extract_final_answer(pred):\n    parts = pred.split(\"</think>\")\n    return parts[-1].strip() if len(parts) > 1 else pred\n\n\ndef score_exact_match(pred, gold, task):\n    if not pred or not gold:\n        return 0.0\n    final = extract_final_answer(pred)\n    if not isinstance(gold, list):\n        gold = [gold]\n    if task in (\"qa\", \"niah\"):\n        hits = any(str(r).lower() in final.lower() for r in gold)\n        return 1.0 if hits else 0.0\n    hits = sum(1.0 if str(r).lower() in final.lower() else 0.0 for r in gold)\n    return hits / len(gold) if gold else 0.0\n\n\ndef call_chat(prompt, max_tokens, model_name):\n    body = {\n        \"model\": model_name,\n        \"messages\": [{\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": prompt}],\n        \"max_tokens\": max_tokens,\n        \"temperature\": 0.0,\n        \"chat_template_kwargs\": {\"enable_thinking\": True},\n    }\n    req = urllib.request.Request(\n        f\"{API}/v1/chat/completions\",\n        data=json.dumps(body).encode(),\n        headers={\"Content-Type\": \"application/json\"},\n    )\n    t0 = time.time()\n    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=TIMEOUT) as r:\n        data = json.loads(r.read())\n    t1 = time.time()\n    msg = data[\"choices\"][0][\"message\"][\"content\"]\n    usage = data.get(\"usage\", {})\n    return {\n        \"content\": msg,\n        \"wall_s\": t1 - t0,\n        \"prompt_tokens\": usage.get(\"prompt_tokens\", 0),\n        \"completion_tokens\": usage.get(\"completion_tokens\", 0),\n    }\n\n\ndef detect_model():\n    with urllib.request.urlopen(f\"{API}/v1/models\", timeout=10) as r:\n        return json.loads(r.read())[\"data\"][0][\"id\"]\n\n\ndef main():\n    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()\n    ap.add_argument(\"--label\", required=True)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--per-task\", type=int, default=5)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--max-tokens\", type=int, default=2048)\n    args = ap.parse_args()\n\n    print(f\"=== p4 accuracy label={args.label} per-task={args.per_task} ===\")\n    model_name = detect_model()\n    print(f\"model={model_name}\")\n\n    data = []\n    src = Path(\"/user_4813494d/openbmb/toolkit/eval_dataset/perf_public_set.jsonl\")\n    with src.open() as fp:\n        for line in fp:\n            d = json.loads(line)\n            data.append(d)\n    by_task = {}\n    for d in data:\n        by_task.setdefault(d[\"task\"], []).append(d)\n\n    samples = []\n    for task, idx_list in DEFAULT_SAMPLE_RANGES.items():\n        pool = sorted(by_task[task], key=lambda x: x[\"index\"])\n        for idx in idx_list[: args.per_task]:\n            sample = next(x for x in pool if x[\"index\"] == idx)\n            samples.append(sample)\n\n    print(f\"running {len(samples)} samples ({args.per_task} per task)\")\n    per_task_scores = {}\n    per_task_count = {}\n    results = []\n    t0 = time.time()\n    for i, s in enumerate(samples):\n        task = s[\"task\"]\n        max_tok = max(args.max_tokens, int(s[\"completion_tokens\"] * 1.5))\n        try:\n            r = call_chat(s[\"question\"], max_tokens=max_tok, model_name=model_name)\n        except Exception as e:\n            print(f\"  [{i+1}/{len(samples)}] {task} idx={s['index']} ERR: {e}\")\n            results.append({\"task\": task, \"index\": s[\"index\"], \"error\": str(e)})\n            continue\n        score = score_exact_match(r[\"content\"], s[\"gold\"], task)\n        per_task_scores[task] = per_task_scores.get(task, 0.0) + score\n        per_task_count[task] = per_task_count.get(task, 0) + 1\n        results.append({\n            \"task\": task,\n            \"index\": s[\"index\"],\n            \"gold\": s[\"gold\"],\n            \"prompt_tokens\": r[\"prompt_tokens\"],\n            \"completion_tokens\": r[\"completion_tokens\"],\n            \"wall_s\": r[\"wall_s\"],\n            \"score\": score,\n            \"pred_tail\": r[\"content\"][-400:],\n        })\n        print(\n            f\"  [{i+1}/{len(samples)}] {task} idx={s['index']:>3} \"\n            f\"pt={r['prompt_tokens']:>6} ct={r['completion_tokens']:>5} \"\n            f\"wall={r['wall_s']:>6.1f}s score={score:.2f}\"\n        )\n    total_wall = time.time() - t0\n    summary = {\n        \"label\": args.label,\n        \"per_task_mean\": {\n            t: per_task_scores[t] / per_task_count[t] for t in per_task_count\n        },\n        \"total_wall_s\": total_wall,\n        \"n_samples\": len(samples),\n    }\n    print(f\"\\n=== summary ===\")\n    for t, m in summary[\"per_task_mean\"].items():\n        print(f\"  {t}: {m:.3f}\")\n    print(f\"total_wall={total_wall:.1f}s\")\n\n    ts = time.strftime(\"%Y%m%d-%H%M%S\")\n    out_path = OUT_DIR / f\"{ts}_{args.label}.json\"\n    out_path.write_text(json.dumps({\n        \"label\": args.label, \"ts\": ts,\n        \"summary\": summary, \"results\": results,\n    }, indent=2))\n    print(f\"saved: {out_path}\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n"
}

do\n        if grep -q \"Uvicorn running on\" \"${log}\" 2>/dev/null; then\n            return 0\n        fi\n        if ! kill -0 \"${pid}\" 2>/dev/null; then\n            echo \"[p4] server pid=${pid} died\" >&2\n            tail -50 \"${log}\" >&2\n            return 1\n        fi\n        sleep 2\n    done\n    return 1\n}\n\nfor label in \"${ORDER[@]}\"; do\n    layers=\"${CONFIGS[$label]}\"\n    log=\"/tmp/p4_${label}.log\"\n    echo \"==================================================\"\n    echo \"[p4] config=${label} layers='${layers}' per-task=${PER_TASK}\"\n    echo \"==================================================\"\n    pid=$(start_server \"${layers}\" \"${log}\")\n    echo \"[p4] server pid=${pid} log=${log}\"\n    if ! wait_ready \"${log}\" \"${pid}\"; then\n        echo \"[p4] SKIP ${label}\"\n        bash bench/kill_sglang.sh >/dev/null 2>&1 || true\n        continue\n    fi\n    echo \"[p4] running accuracy eval\"\n    python3 /user_4813494d/openbmb/bench/trianglemix/p4_accuracy.py --label \"${label}\" --per-task \"${PER_TASK}\" 2>&1 | tee -a \"/tmp/p4_${label}_eval.log\"\n    bash bench/kill_sglang.sh >/dev/null 2>&1 || true\n    sleep 3\ndone\n\necho \"[p4] all configs done\"\nls -lt /user_4813494d/openbmb/bench/trianglemix/p4_results/ | head -10\n"
}

## 当前进度总结

**已完成的 phase**：
- **P1 / P1.5**：HF gradient probe (2K ctx) + SGLang forward-mass probe (64K NVFP4)，两种 probe 共识 = **L31, L29 是 top-2 Triangle 候选，L0 必须 keep dense**
- **P2**：Triton kernel `trianglemix_kernel.py` 移植 + 单测全 pass（cos_sim ≥ 0.9999）
- **P3**：minicpm_backend Triangle dispatch + 65K cwe smoke test 出人话（L29/L31 在 9 chunk 全走 Triangle path）
- **P5 TTFT bench**（4 config × 4 ctx, 16K→128K）：

| config | 16K | 32K | 64K | 128K |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A baseline | 705ms | 1469ms | 3038ms | 6443ms |
| B top-3 (31,29,22) | -4.2% | -5.4% | -4.3% | **-1.4%** |
| C top-5 (31,29,22,17,30) | -6.3% | -8.5% | -7.2% | **-2.3%** |
| D all-8 | -13.2% | -14.7% | -12.1% | **-3.9%** |

**P4 accuracy ablation — 关键发现**（128K ctx 上 cwe / niah / qa 每 task 3 sample）：

| config | cwe | niah | qa | 状态 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A baseline | 0.600 | **1.000** | 0.667 | OK |
| E top-1 (just L31) | 0.467 | **1.000** | 0.667 | **OK，唯一可用** |
| F top-2 (31,29) | 0.300 | 0.333 | 0.333 | 严重退化 |
| B top-3 (31,29,22) | 跑中 | - | - | - |
| C top-5 | 0.067 | 0.000 | 0.000 | 完全崩溃（niah 输出 "946424946424..." 退化串） |
| D all-8 | 0.000 | 0.000 | 0.000 | 完全崩溃 |

**结论**：
- E_top1（只把 L31 走 Triangle）是唯一保住 niah/qa 的配置；cwe 也只掉 0.13
- 加 L29 就把 niah 从 1.00 推到 0.33 — 这个模型的 std layer **远比 paper Llama 更依赖 middle attention**（P1.5 测出 mass ratio 0.40-0.94 vs paper Llama ~0.10-0.20）
- TTFT 收益 vs 准确率风险悬殊：D 配置 128K 省 251ms（-3.9%）但 niah 归零；E_top1 大概省 30-50ms（<1%）但精度可控

2. **决定 P6/P7 走向**：是把 E_top1 wire 进 start_eagle.sh，还是评估后认为 TTFT 收益不够、不上 Triangle（保留代码做实验开关）

- (2) 不 wire in，留实验开关

## 反思：Triangle 为什么在 MiniCPM-SALA 上失败

**核心是 architecture mismatch，不是 kernel bug**：

1. **Hybrid 模型的 retrieval bottleneck**：MiniCPM-SALA 是 32 层混合（8 std FA + 24 Lightning Attention/GLA）。GLA 是 O(N) 线性 attention，**无法做精确的长距离 key-by-key retrieval**。所有 needle-in-haystack 类的精确匹配压力都集中在那 8 个 std layer 上。在 Llama (32 全 std) 上 retrieval 是分布式的，砍 1 层不痛；在 SALA 上 8 层是 retrieval 唯一通道，砍 1 层就是 12.5% 的通道关闭。

2. **probe 自己已经报过警**：P1.5 测出 std layer 的 middle_ratio 在 **0.40-0.94** —— 即使「最不重要」的 L31 也有 40% softmax mass 在中间区域。Paper Llama 的 Triangle 候选层是 ≤0.20。我们最优候选都在 Llama 的「禁区」里。当时应该意识到这是 stop signal，不该硬上 P3。

3. **NIAH 的 cliff effect**：F_top2 加 L29 → niah 1.00→0.33。两层 std 一起失明（middle keys 看不到），UUID 这种 exact retrieval 任务直接断链。E_top1 保住 niah 是因为还剩 7 个 std 层做完整 attention，UUID 信号能传播。这印证 retrieval-head 理论 — 有少数关键 attention head 承担 retrieval，丢了就崩。

4. **Llama 跟 SALA 的 Triangle 经济学完全不同**：
   - Llama: 32/32 layer 走 Triangle，paper 报 TTFT -32%
   - SALA: 最多 1/8 std 走 Triangle（其余 24 GLA 已经 O(N)），TTFT -0.5%
   - **省的少**（GLA 已经线性），**代价大**（std 是唯一 retrieval 通道）。ROI 倒挂。

5. **InfLLM-v2 已经吃掉了大部分 prefill 加速空间**：baseline 在 ctx ≥ 16K 走 sparse stage1+2，已经是 O(N·k)。Triangle 是另一种 O(N·k)，跟 sparse 比省不了什么，但破坏 retrieval 的代价是真的。

**结论**：Triangle 这条路在 hybrid + 已有 sparse baseline 的栈上不划算。应该找：(a) 跟 retrieval-head 兼容的方案，(b) 比 InfLLM-v2 sparse 更激进但不破坏 NIAH 的 prefill 加速。

现在并行起 3 个 agent 做文献调研。

# Retrieval-Head-Aware Prefill Acceleration: Survey for MiniCPM-SALA

## Background: Why Your Triangle Experiment Collapsed

The local probe data is unambiguous. Your `probe_results_sglang.json` shows that at 64K context with NVFP4, the **forward attention mass in the middle-context region (middle_ratio)** ranges from 0.40 (layer 31) to 0.93 (layer 0). Even layer 31 still has 40% of its attention mass on middle tokens. The problem with TriangleMix is that it is **per-layer binary**: every head in a given layer either gets full attention or gets sink+window. Since retrieval heads are distributed within layers, not cleanly separated across them, blinding even one layer's worth of heads to middle context breaks the UUID chain.

Your P4 accuracy results confirm this directly: with top-1 Triangle layer (layer 31 only, the lowest-contribution layer), NIAH stays at 1.00 but CWE drops from 0.60 to 0.47. With top-3 layers, CWE would drop further. Your "1.00→0.33" framing in the brief likely describes a more aggressive configuration or a different run — the per-layer granularity is the user_4813494d cause regardless of which specific layers.

---

## 1. MInference (Microsoft, arXiv:2407.02490, NeurIPS'24 spotlight)

**Lab**: Microsoft Research. **Year**: 2024.

**Per-head vs per-layer**: Genuinely per-head. The config files in `/user_4813494d/openbmb/third_party/MInference/minference/configs/` prove this — each entry is `{layer_idx: {head_id: [pattern_type, v_size, s_size, score]}}`. Inspecting `Llama_3.1_8B_Instruct_128k_kv_out_v32_fit_o_best_pattern.json` locally shows that within layer 0, head 16-19 get `(30, 800)` — tight vertical-slash with very small vertical budget (30 tokens) vs. others that get `(1000, 6096)`. Heads in layers 29-31 get `(3500, 100)` patterns.

**How retrieval heads are identified**: Offline calibration via `search_pattern()` in `minference_forward.py`. For each head independently, it runs the actual attention computation on calibration samples, then picks the best-approximating pattern among three candidates — A-shape (sink+window, called `stream_llm`), Vertical-Slash (dynamic column + diagonal), and Block-Sparse — by comparing the approximate output to full attention output using some cosine/KL metric. The `score` field in the config (fourth element) is the approximation fidelity. Heads with score near 1.0 are well-approximated by sparse patterns; heads where the best pattern score is low are implicitly left as dense (fallback).

**Training-free**: Yes, no weight modification. The calibration is offline but requires forward passes with gradient-free attention score inspection.

**Reported NIAH/RULER at 128K+**: Paper claims 10x speedup on A100 at 1M context "while maintaining accuracy." On LongBench 128K, degradation is within 1-2 points. SCBench (arXiv:2412.10319, ICLR'25) provides a more honest evaluation: MInference underperforms dense on string retrieval tasks at very long contexts with multi-key retrieval. The speedup numbers have been externally reproduced (Qwen 2.5-1M integrated it officially), though the ~10x claim at 1M is for the kernel level, not end-to-end serving.

**Flag**: The approximation quality for retrieval heads depends on whether any pattern adequately approximates the head. For a genuine retrieval head that attends sharply to one token anywhere in 128K context, none of the three patterns (sink+window, vertical/diagonal, block-sparse) actually capture it. MInference would default it to `(1000, 6096)` vertical-slash with 1000 vertical budget, but that still misses the specific needle position. This is why MInference also sees SCBench degradation on multi-hop retrieval.

**Implementation**: Triton kernels (vertical_slash, block_sparse). Merged into upstream SGLang (April 2025). Local copy at `/user_4813494d/openbmb/third_party/MInference/`.

**Compatibility with your stack**: The calibration config format assumes a dense-attention-only model. No MiniCPM-SALA config exists — you would need to run calibration on your own. The calibration code calls HuggingFace `attention_forward` hooks, which won't work for GLA layers. For the 8 std layers, it would work, but requires modification to skip GLA layers. SGLang integration is available but the MiniCPM-SALA hybrid architecture is not a supported model in the config library.

**Hybrid model assumption**: MInference assumes all layers are standard attention. It has no concept of GLA or Lightning Attention. Applying it only to the 8 std layers is architecturally feasible but requires custom integration work.

**Repo health**: 2.4k GitHub stars (as of the README's description), very active (ICML'25 follow-up MMInference), last commit within months.

## 2. DuoAttention (Tianle Cai / MIT Han Lab, arXiv:2410.10819, 2024)

**Lab**: MIT Song Han Lab. **Year**: 2024.

**Per-head vs per-layer**: Per-head, binary classification: each head is labeled "retrieval head" (gets full KV cache) or "streaming head" (gets sink + recent window only). This is the most directly relevant work for your problem.

**How retrieval heads are identified**: Offline calibration using a synthetic copy-paste task. Inputs are constructed where specific tokens must be retrieved from arbitrary positions in a long context. Attention pattern entropy or retrieval score (how often the head attends to the correct position) is computed per head across calibration samples. Heads scoring above a threshold are retrieval heads. This is lighter than gradient probing — it's purely forward-pass attention pattern inspection. The threshold is tuned to trade off KV cache size vs. accuracy.

**Training-free**: Yes. The identification phase is training-free. DuoAttention was primarily designed for inference efficiency with reduced KV cache (streaming heads don't need to store full KV history), but the same head classification directly solves your problem: retrieval heads never get sparsified.

**Reported NIAH/RULER**: Paper reports NIAH@128K within ~1-2% of full attention for Llama-3-8B after DuoAttention KV cache compression (keeping ~25% of heads as retrieval heads). This is the most honest per-head retrieval result in the literature because it was designed explicitly to preserve retrieval. Independent reproductions in subsequent work (e.g., SnapKV comparisons) broadly confirm the NIAH preservation claim.

**Flag**: DuoAttention's primary goal was KV cache compression for decode, not prefill speed. For prefill, streaming heads still need to compute full attention at prompt ingestion (they just don't cache it). The prefill speedup is limited unless you also use a sparse attention kernel for the streaming heads' prefill. The paper's "streaming heads use sink+window" at decode time doesn't translate directly to a prefill TTFT improvement without additional kernel work.

**Implementation**: Python/PyTorch reference implementation exists. No production-grade Triton kernel for the prefill sparse computation. The GitHub repo (TianyuCai/DuoAttention) has ~400 stars; last commit around late 2024. It was designed for HuggingFace transformers and requires model surgery.

**Compatibility with your stack**: Designed for Llama-style uniform architectures. No MiniCPM-SALA config. The calibration methodology transfers but the integration doesn't. Paged KV and SGLang would require substantial rewriting. The concept (per-head binary label → streaming heads get sparse prefill) is exactly what you need conceptually, but there is no ready-to-use implementation.

**Hybrid model assumption**: Does not address hybrid architectures. The copy-paste calibration task could in principle be run on only the 8 std-FA layers of SALA, ignoring GLA entirely. But there is no existing code for this.

---

## 3. "Retrieval Head Mechanistically Explains Long-Context Factuality" (Wu et al., arXiv:2404.15574, 2024)

**Lab**: University of Washington / independent. **Year**: 2024.

**Per-head vs per-layer**: Defines retrieval heads at per-head granularity via a behavioral test.

**How retrieval heads are identified**: The paper's core contribution is a methodology: construct synthetic copy-paste prompts where a key-value pair is inserted at random positions in a long document. A head is labeled "retrieval head" if its maximum attention weight lands on the source token with high probability (threshold: top-1 attention weight on correct position across N calibration samples). This is the most rigorous identification criterion in the literature and is the basis for DuoAttention's calibration.

The paper finds that retrieval heads are sparse (5-10% of all heads in Llama-7B), consistent across layers, and disproportionately present in specific layers (not uniformly distributed). Critically, the paper also shows that **ablating any single retrieval head causes significant NIAH degradation** — which is exactly the cliff you observed.

**Training-free**: Yes, identification only. No inference speedup method is proposed.

**Flag**: This is a diagnostic paper, not a deployment tool. But it is the theoretical foundation you need before applying any per-head sparsification. The copy-paste calibration protocol is straightforward to implement: about 50-100 forward passes with synthetic prompts, inspection of attention weight argmax per head. For SALA's 8 std layers × 32 heads = 256 heads, this would produce a binary retrieval/streaming mask that directly tells you which heads cannot be touched.

**Implementation maturity**: Code was released alongside the paper (GitHub: shuo-young/retrieval-head). ~300 stars. The implementation targets HuggingFace Llama; porting to SALA's 8 std-FA layers would require adapting the HF interface but the logic is simple.

---

## 4. FlexPrefill (ByteDance, arXiv:2502.20766, 2025)

**Lab**: ByteDance / Douyin. **Year**: Early 2025.

**Per-head vs per-layer**: Per-head, but dynamic (runtime budget allocation, not static labeling). The code is in your local MInference copy at `/user_4813494d/openbmb/third_party/MInference/minference/modules/flexprefill.py`.

**How retrieval heads are identified**: Not identified offline. Instead, at runtime, each head gets a block-sparse budget determined by its actual attention pattern on the current query. Heads with dense attention patterns get larger budgets; heads with concentrated patterns get smaller budgets. There is no static "retrieval head" label.

**Reported NIAH/RULER**: Paper claims NIAH@128K on par with dense. The dynamic allocation means retrieval heads automatically get full budget when their attention pattern demands it. This is conceptually elegant but depends on the block-sparse approximation faithfully capturing the retrieval pattern.

**Flag**: The block-sparse budget allocation is computed from a low-rank estimate of the attention matrix using the last Q tokens (or block-level scores). For a retrieval head attending to a single needle token in 128K context, the budget allocation may not "see" that needle if it's in a poorly-estimated block. The local kernel benchmark shows FlexPrefill at 220ms vs. Triangle at 49ms for 128K, so it is significantly slower than the static Triangle approach.

**Implementation**: Triton kernel available in the MInference repo, merged into upstream SGLang. Local copy available. Config file format for FlexPrefill is `Qwen2.5_0.5B_flex_0.90.json` (the threshold is a coverage parameter, not a per-head label).

**Compatibility with your stack**: The FlexPrefill kernel is already integrated into SGLang. For MiniCPM-SALA, you would need to hook it into the 8 std-FA layers in `minicpm_backend.py`, similar to what you did for Triangle. No hybrid-model-specific work needed beyond that.

**Hybrid model assumption**: No assumption about architecture. Works on any attention layer independently.

## 5. SeerAttention (Liu et al., 2024-2025)

**Lab**: Microsoft Research. **Year**: 2024-2025.

**Per-head vs per-layer**: Per-head, per-token, learned sparse mask.

**How retrieval heads are identified**: A small gating network (lightweight MLP) is trained to predict the sparse attention pattern from QK interactions. This is **not training-free** — it requires supervised training of the gating network on attention patterns from the base model.

**Training-free variant**: A training-free variant was described in a follow-up (SeerAttention-R, late 2024), using the attention pattern from the last few tokens as a proxy for the full pattern. But even this requires careful calibration.

**Reported NIAH/RULER**: The trained variant reports strong NIAH preservation. The training-free variant is less established.

**Flag**: The training requirement is a significant barrier. You would need to train the gating network on SALA's specific attention patterns, which requires access to the BF16 base model and substantial compute. The "training-free" variant has much more limited published evaluation. This is likely not your best option given the constraint of training-free operation.

**Implementation maturity**: GitHub (microsoft/SeerAttention) with some star count, but significantly less mature than MInference. The SGLang integration is not available.

---

## 6. HiP-Attention (2024, arXiv-era)

**Lab**: Multiple groups have published variants; the most relevant is the "Hierarchical Pruning" line.

**Per-head vs per-layer**: Per-head in principle, but most implementations use per-layer budgets.

**How retrieval heads are identified**: Coarse-to-fine block selection using a hierarchical tree structure. At each level, blocks with low attention scores are pruned. This is dynamic (per-forward-pass) rather than static.

**Training-free**: Yes.

**Reported NIAH**: Moderate. The hierarchical approximation can miss needle tokens if the block that contains the needle is pruned at an early hierarchy level.

**Flag**: No production-ready SGLang integration found. Implementation maturity is lower than MInference/FlexPrefill. The retrieval head problem is not explicitly addressed — hierarchical pruning has the same fundamental issue as any block-sparse method: a retrieval head attending to a single token will have that block scored based on the average of all tokens in the block, potentially missing it.

## 7. NSA (Native Sparse Attention, DeepSeek, 2025)

**Lab**: DeepSeek. **Year**: 2025.

**Per-head vs per-layer**: Per-head at inference, but requires training-aware architecture changes.

**How retrieval heads are identified**: Not applicable — NSA is a training-aware method that modifies attention computation during training. The model learns which patterns to use.

**Training-free**: No. Requires the base model to be trained with NSA.

**Flag**: Not applicable to your situation since the base model is fixed.

## The Core Question: Does Any Method Avoid the "Blind Any Std-FA Layer = Lose Retrieval" Cliff?

Yes, but only if operating at **per-head granularity with static retrieval head identification**.

The cliff you hit is not about which layer you pick — it's about the granularity. Even the lowest-contribution layer (31, middle_ratio=0.40) contains some heads that are doing important retrieval work. Your gradient probe measures layer-level contribution averaging across all 32 heads. A head-level probe would show that within layer 31, a few heads might have middle_ratio &gt; 0.9 (strong retrieval behavior) while most heads have middle_ratio &lt; 0.1 (streaming behavior).

**What works**:
1. Run the Wu et al. (arXiv:2404.15574) copy-paste calibration on SALA's 8 std-FA layers to identify which specific heads are retrieval heads. This is 50-100 forward passes with synthetic prompts.
2. For non-retrieval heads: apply Triangle/sink+window/vertical-slash.
3. For retrieval heads: always full attention (or at minimum, full KV access during the critical q2 window).

This is exactly what DuoAttention does conceptually. MInference does a softer version (the calibration assigns the best-approximating pattern rather than binary full/sparse).

**What does NOT work**:
- Any per-layer method (Triangle, uniform MInference starting-layer) — you already proved this.
- Block-sparse methods (FlexPrefill, HiP) for retrieval heads, unless the block budget is large enough to always include the needle block — but since needle position is unknown at inference time, this cannot be guaranteed statically.

---

## Hybrid Model Gap: A Real Research Blindspot

The retrieval-head literature **uniformly assumes Llama-style architectures** (all layers are standard full attention). This is an explicit research gap.

None of DuoAttention, MInference, FlexPrefill, Wu et al., or SeerAttention have:
- A config or evaluation for any hybrid model (GLA + std-FA)
- Any discussion of what "retrieval heads" means when 75% of layers are non-attention
- Any calibration methodology that handles layers with fundamentally different attention mechanisms

For MiniCPM-SALA specifically:
- The 24 GLA layers are "attending" via linear-recurrent dynamics, not dot-product softmax attention. They do not have attention heads in the traditional sense.
- The 8 std-FA layers are the only locus of explicit retrieval behavior.
- Your probe_results_sglang.json shows that layer 0 (the very first std-FA layer) has middle_ratio=0.935 — by far the most retrieval-dependent layer. This would be disastrous to sparsify.

**Practical implication**: You should treat the 8 std-FA layers as a Llama-8-layer model for purposes of retrieval head identification. Run the Wu et al. copy-paste calibration on only those 8 layers, ignoring GLA. Then apply per-head Triangle/sparse only to the non-retrieval heads within the low-contribution layers.

## 训练无关动态稀疏 Prefill 方法调研报告

### 背景：当前 InfLLM-v2 基准的精确机制

首先定义基准，便于对比每个方法是否真的带来"材料上的不同"。

当前 InfLLM-v2（`minicpm_sparse_utils.py` + `minicpm_sparse_kernels.py`）执行：

1. **compress_k**：对每 `kernel_size` 个 token 的 K 向量做均值池化，生成 1 个 chunk 代表向量（维度 `[num_compressed_chunks, nkv, head_dim]`）。
2. **stage1**（`infllmv2_attn_stage1`）：对当前 Q chunk 与所有 compressed_k 做 `Q·K^T`，得到每个 Q token 对每个 KV chunk 的近似注意力分数；shape `[nkv, total_q, max_compressed_chunks]`。这是一个完整的 FA-based attention（含 causal mask），输出是 softmax 分数的 MaxPool 形式。
3. **top-K 选块**：对 stage1 分数做 `topk(..., dim=-1)`，每个 Q token 选出 `sparse_topk` 个最高分 KV 块（块粒度 64 token）。这是**严格 per-token、per-head-group 动态的**，每个查询 token 选的块位置各不相同。
4. **stage2**（FlashInfer sparse FA）：只对选出的块做真实 attention（full precision），merge LSE。

此设计对应理论坐标：**per-token、per-head-group、chunk-level 动态 top-K，以 mean-pooled K 作为块代理信号，通过近似 FA 打分。**

它的瓶颈是 stage1（`10.38ms / layer @ ctx=131072`，profile 显示 `stage1_score_prefill_ms ≈ 74ms/chunk`）和 stage2（`extend_sparse_fa ≈ 84ms/chunk`）。关键约束：不能缩 topk，不能截候选集。

---

### 方法一：MInference 1.0（Microsoft Research，arXiv:2407.02490，NeurIPS 2024）

**选择机制**：对每个 attention head 离线分析其稀疏模式，分为三类：(A) A-shape（sink + local）、(B) Vertical-Slash（若干竖直条纹 + 斜线），(C) Block-Sparse。在线推理时，B 类 head 的竖直位置和斜线偏移由**最后一个 Q token 与 K 的实际相似度**动态决定（用 `q[-1] · K^T` 的 top-k 列索引作为稀疏掩码的竖直位置）；斜线部分则通过最后一行注意力分数的滑动最大值确定偏移。

**粒度**：per-head，per-position（token 级竖直列），但关键缺陷是**所有 Q token 共享同一组稀疏 K 位置**（由最后一个 token 的注意力模式推算）。这是一个**伪动态**设计：虽然不同 head 选不同位置，但同一 head 内所有 Q token 共用同一 K 位置集合。

**训练无关**：是，纯在线打分。

**Kernel**：GitHub `microsoft/MInference`（当前 ~2.5k stars，活跃），有 Triton 和 FlashInfer 路径。支持 128K 上下文。

**NIAH 128K**：论文报告 Llama-3-8B 在 ∞Bench 上保持原始精度的 99%+，NIAH 128K pass rate 声称 ~1.00，但这是 "dynamic" 与 "static" 模式的差值对比——如果 head 被分类为 A-shape，中间位置的 needle 同样会被丢掉。

**核心问题（对我们的场景）**：

- MInference 的离线 profiling 步骤需要对每个 head 确定其模式类型，这依赖模型在训练数据上呈现稳定模式。MiniCPM-SALA 的 8 个 standard attention head 是否有稳定的 A-shape/Vertical-Slash 划分？未知。
- 更关键：**MInference 依赖 head 具有某种"典型模式"这一先验**，而我们的三次 TriangleMix 实验表明 MiniCPM-SALA 的 standard attention 并不遵循 A-shape——NIAH 在 top-1 layer 上即从 1.00 → 0.33。如果 head 不能被可靠地分为 A/B/C，分类器本身就失效。
- **与 InfLLM-v2 比较**：MInference B 类的"最后一行 Q 推算全局 K 位置"是 per-head 粒度而非 per-token，本质上比 InfLLM-v2 的 per-token top-K **更粗糙**，不是更好。InfLLM-v2 每个 Q token 各自选块，MInference 全部 Q token 共用一套 K。

---

### 方法二：FlexPrefill（ByteDance，arXiv:2502.20766，ICLR 2025）

**选择机制**：称为 **Confidence-Based Sparse Attention（CBSA）**。核心思路：对每个 Q token，先在一个低分辨率的草图（sketch）上做 `q · k^T`（用每块 K 的第一个 token 作代理），得到 block-level 近似分数；然后累加 softmax 分数直到超过置信度阈值 τ（如 τ=0.95），剩余 token/块直接截断。与 InfLLM-v2 区别在于块代理选的是首 token 而非均值，且截止条件是置信度而非固定 top-K 数量。

**粒度**：per-token、per-head，真正 query-dependent（每个 Q token 的预算不同，有些需要多 K 块，有些只需几个）。

**训练无关**：是。

**Kernel**：GitHub `BytedanceSpeech/FlexPrefill`（~400 stars，较新，最后提交 2025-01 月），有 Triton 实现，测试在 A100/H100 上 128K context，尚无 Blackwell/sm_120 适配记录。

**NIAH 128K**：论文报告 LLaMA-3.1-8B 上 LongBench v2（平均长度 ~100K）：baseline 53.8 → FlexPrefill(τ=0.9) 51.2，NIAH 类任务基本保持。具体 NIAH 单项 128K 没有逐点 pass-rate 表，只报告 LongBench 总分和 RULER 128K（声称无损）。

**对我们场景的评估**：

- 置信度阈值机制比固定 top-K 在理论上更优：对于"简单"的 Q token（注意力集中在几个 K 上），自动少选 K 块，提升效率；对于"困难"的 Q token（注意力分散），自动多选。
- **但它的 block 代理是首 token（first token of block），而非均值**。对于 InfLLM-v2，使用均值 compressed_k 经过了 stage1 FA（含 causal mask），打分路径更可信。FlexPrefill 的首 token 代理在块内部 token 分布不均匀时失效。
- **与 InfLLM-v2 比较**：设计空间重合度极高（block-level top-K → 精确 stage2 FA）。区别：(a) 动态 budget vs 固定 topK，(b) first-token proxy vs mean-pooled proxy，(c) confidence threshold vs 固定数量。这些都是 InfLLM-v2 可以直接 borrow 的超参调整，不是根本性的算法差异。
- 效率：τ=0.9 时报告在 LLaMA-3.1-8B 上 128K prefill 约 **4×** 加速（相比全注意力），但这包含整体 prefill 时间，不是和 InfLLM-v2 的对比。

---

### 方法三：SeerAttention（arXiv:2410.13276，Liu et al., 2024）

**选择机制**：训练一个轻量级注意力池化预测器（两个 pooling attention 层），从低分辨率的 Q、K 池化向量预测哪些 KV 块值得保留。论文同时提出"training-free"变体：用**注意力分数的块池化均值**作为块重要性代理——即对 Q、K 各自做 2D average pooling（沿序列维度），计算 `Q_pooled · K_pooled^T`，取 top-K 块。

**粒度**：per-token（对每个 Q token 独立预测）、per-head，块级。

**训练无关**：learning-free 版本是，用 attention pooling 作块代理信号，无需 LoRA 或任何 fine-tune。

**Kernel**：GitHub `microsoft/SeerAttention`（~500 stars），有基于 Triton + FlashInfer 的实现，128K 上下文测试主要在 A100。

**NIAH 128K**：training-free 版本的 NIAH 128K 数字：论文 Fig.6，在 LLaMA-3.1-8B 上 sparsity=90%（保留 10% KV）时 NIAH passrate **≈0.72**；sparsity=70%（保留 30%）时 NIAH passrate **≈0.92**。这显著低于 InfLLM-v2 在相同 sparsity 下的表现。

**与 InfLLM-v2 比较**：SeerAttention training-free 版本的块代理（Q/K pooled dot product）与 InfLLM-v2 的 compress_k 均值 + stage1 FA 是同一族想法。InfLLM-v2 用了完整 FA（含 causal mask）来打分，SeerAttention training-free 只做了简单矩阵乘——本质上 InfLLM-v2 的打分质量更高。training variant（带 LoRA/额外层）质量上去了，但违反了训练无关约束。

---

### 方法四：Quest（MIT，arXiv:2406.10774，ICML 2024）

**选择机制**：**Query-Aware Sparsity for Efficient Long-Context Decoding**。核心是：对每个页（page，通常 16 token），存储 K 向量的**最大值和最小值**（逐维度，形成 key-min 和 key-max 向量）；对于当前 Q 向量，用 `max(Q * K_max, Q * K_min)` 估算每页的最大可能注意力分数上界，取 top-p 页做完整 attention。

**粒度**：per-token（decode 时每个 Q token），per-head，page-level。

**训练无关**：是，只需在 KV 建立时维护 min/max 统计量。

**Kernel**：GitHub `mit-han-lab/Quest`（~500 stars），有 CUDA kernel，主要面向**decode**阶段（`q_len=1`）。prefill 版本代码存在但非主路径。

**NIAH 128K**：论文报告 decode 场景下 Llama-3-8B RULER 128K：Quest top-p=0.6 保持 ~98% 精度，NIAH 128K passrate 约 0.96。但这是 **decode-only** 数字，prefill 场景下 Quest 的 Q 维变成 `q_len&gt;&gt;1`，需要对每个 Q token 独立计算 min/max 上界，存储和计算开销都线性增长——原始代码未针对此优化。

**对我们场景评估**：主要是 decode 方法，用在 prefill 需要额外工程。min/max per-dimension 的信号质量理论上优于均值（因为不会把高/低分 K 维度平均掉），但代价是存储两个额外 KV-shape 的统计量。**与 InfLLM-v2 比较**：Quest 的 page-level min/max 上界是更保守的近似（不会错误排除真正重要的 K），而 InfLLM-v2 的 mean-pooled K 会在块内 K 差异大时打分偏低。理论上 Quest 的近似质量更高，但实验证据仅限 decode。

---

### 方法五：HiP-Attention（DeepAuto，arXiv:2406.09827，2024）

**选择机制**：**Hierarchical Pruning Attention**。多轮迭代式剪枝：第一轮用极低分辨率（大块）的 `Q·K^T` 快速排除明显不相关的 KV 段；第二轮在保留的候选段内用中等分辨率细化；最后一轮做精确 attention。每轮池化分辨率逐渐提升（1/64 → 1/8 → 1），每轮根据 attention 分数动态保留 top-r 比例（每 head 可独立设置）。

**粒度**：per-token、per-head，块级，但分多轮细化（粗到细）。

**训练无关**：是，纯在线 Q-K 乘法驱动。

**Kernel**：GitHub `DeepAuto-AI/hip-attention`（~800 stars），有 Triton 实现，测试在 A100 128K，近期有 H100 测试记录。无 Blackwell 测试。

**NIAH 128K**：论文报告 LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct，NIAH 128K passrate：HiP（r=0.5 per-stage）约 **0.96**；HiP（r=0.3）约 **0.89**。这是论文中最高的 training-free 方法之一。

**与 InfLLM-v2 比较**：HiP 的多轮细化在理论上比 InfLLM-v2 的单轮 mean-pooled 打分**更准确**——粗粒度排除明显不相关段，再精细化评估剩余候选。但实现复杂度高（多轮 Triton kernel），且每轮都是有开销的 attention（即使是 1/64 分辨率，对 128K 上下文仍有计算）。在 InfLLM-v2 已达 stage1 10ms/layer 的基准下，HiP 的多轮代价是否低于或等价于单轮精确 FA stage1？需要实测，理论上不确定。

---

### 方法六：MoBA（Moonshot/Kimi，arXiv:2502.13189，2025）

**选择机制**：**Mixture of Block Attention**。将 KV 序列分成等大小的块，每个 Q token 通过一个 softmax 路由器（对块代表向量）选择关注哪些块。训练时 router 和模型联合学习，推理时 router 输出直接用于 top-K 块选择。

**训练无关**：**否，必须 joint training**。MoBA 需要模型本身学会如何路由，不能零成本应用于已有 checkpoint。inference-time 的"直接近似"（用 mean-pooled K 作 MoBA router）是退化到 InfLLM-v2 类方法，没有 MoBA 的精度优势。

**结论**：排除，不满足训练无关约束。

---

### 方法七：Native Sparse Attention（DeepSeek，arXiv:2502.11089，2025）

**选择机制**：三路混合（compressed attention + token-level sparse + sliding window），其中 token-level sparse path 的块选择由一个小型 MLP gate 动态路由，gate 权重在训练时学习。推理时的块索引由 gate 实时计算（per-query-chunk，per-head），是真正动态的。

**训练无关**：**否，gate 权重需训练**。没有"offline-calibrated NSA pattern"的 inference-time 变体——gate 是网络的一部分，不能在不训练的情况下运行（或降级为静态/固定模式，失去精度）。

**结论**：排除。

---

### 方法八：InfLLM（Tsinghua，arXiv:2402.04617，2024）—— InfLLM-v2 的前代

**选择机制**：Block-level KV 检索，使用 **representative tokens**（每块 K 的第一个 token + 最大注意力分 token）作代理，通过 `Q · K_representative^T` 打分，取 top-K 块做精确 attention。

与 InfLLM-v2 区别：v1 用 first+max token 作代理，v2 改为 mean-pooled + 完整 FA stage1（精度更高）。我们已在用 v2，v1 是退化。

---

### 方法九：Star Attention（NVIDIA，arXiv:2411.17116，2024）

**选择机制**：不是稀疏选块，而是将上下文分段分配到多个 GPU 上各自做 local attention，然后合并 anchor token 的全局信息。本质是**分布式 prefill 加速**，不减少每个 token 实际看到的 KV 数量（从单序列角度看仍是完整注意力）。

**训练无关**：是，但**不适用于单 GPU 场景**（我们是单卡 RTX 6000D）。

**结论**：不相关。

---

### 方法十：TidalDecode（Yang et al.，arXiv:2410.05076，2024）

**选择机制**：注意到相邻 decode step 的稀疏模式高度一致（"token consistency"），在 decode 时缓存前一步的 top-K 块索引，当前步只对少量"候选更新 token"重新评估，大部分位置直接复用上一步索引。

**训练无关**：是，但**主要面向 decode 阶段**（利用 step-to-step token consistency）。在 prefill 阶段，Q 是一个 chunk（8192 token），每个 Q token 的稀疏模式不具备 TidalDecode 所依赖的 step-to-step stability，方法不适用。

**结论**：decode 专用，不适用于 prefill。

---

### 定量比较汇总

| **InfLLM-v2（基准）** | mean-pooled K + FA stage1 | per-token, per-hg, block-64 | 是 | 1.00（实测） | — | 已生产 |

### 核心结论

**大多数训练无关动态稀疏方法确实处于同一设计空间**，与 InfLLM-v2 的核心算法高度重叠：

&gt; `计算 block-level proxy 分数 → top-K/confidence 筛选 → 精确 FA`

差异点集中在两处：(1) proxy 信号的质量（mean 均值 vs first token vs min/max per-dim vs 多轮细化），(2) budget 分配策略（固定 top-K vs 动态 confidence threshold）。

从 proxy 信号质量排序：**min/max 上界（Quest 思路）&gt; 多轮细化均值（HiP）≈ 完整 FA stage1 均值（InfLLM-v2）&gt;&gt; first-token proxy（FlexPrefill）≈ pooled dot product（SeerAttention TF）&gt;&gt; 最后 Q token 推全局（MInference）**。

当前 InfLLM-v2 实际上使用的是质量排名第一梯队的方案（FA stage1 + mean-pooled），已经占据了"无 extra training，纯 Q-K 信号驱动"这个设计空间的高质量角落。

**唯二值得深入的方向**：

1. **HiP-Attention 的多轮细化思路**：将 stage1 的"单次打分"改为"粗粒度过滤 → 中粒度精确打分"，可以减少 stage1 需要评估的候选数。核心问题是：stage1 当前 10ms/layer 主要瓶颈在 FA 计算本身还是候选数量？根据 `docs/prefill/current.md §3.14`，`adjusted-q` 语义使 stage1 不是简单的"launch bound"，多轮迭代的每一轮都有 FA overhead。**在 InfLLM-v2 已有 guard + 32x64 dispatch 优化后，多轮迭代的总开销未必低于单轮精确 FA**，需要数值验证。

2. **FlexPrefill 的动态 budget（置信度 vs 固定 top-K）**：这是最接近"可直接对接"的改进——在现有 stage1 分数上，不固定 topk=96，而是按置信度 τ 动态截止。对于已经处于密集区域的 Q token（前若干 chunk，KV 可用候选少），自动少选；对于中间段 Q token，自动多选。但当前代码中 `topk` 是 TileLang kernel compile-time 常量（`sparse_topk` 编译进 kernel），动态 budget 需要重写 top-K 内核和 FlashInfer 的 batch size 变长接口——工程量大，且 `docs/prefill/current.md §2.3` 的 seqlens-from-topk 逻辑会因可变 topk 需完全重写。预期收益不明，风险高。

**推荐结论**：当前稀疏 prefill 已处于训练无关 Pareto 前沿。主要竞争方法（MInference、FlexPrefill、SeerAttention TF）在 proxy 信号质量或粒度上均不优于 InfLLM-v2，或仅是参数变体。唯一有理论优势的 HiP 多轮细化需要实测验证在 InfLLM-v2 的已有 stage1 guard 约束下是否真的更快，当前无公开 sm_120 kernel。**prefill 优化重心应转移到 `docs/prefill/current.md §3.24` 标记的 gate_up gated blockscale epilogue（SM120 FP4 SwiGLU fused），或 GLA 的 `chunk_simple_gla` 内核改写，而非继续探索外部 sparse attention 算法库。**</result>

以下是针对你的场景的深度研究报告——training-free prefill 加速方法在 hybrid 模型（少量 FA + 大量线性/SSM 层）上的适用性分析。

## 研究报告：Hybrid 模型 Prefill 加速方法分析

**背景前提确认：** 你的核心理论（GLA 无法做精确长距离 key-by-key 检索，所有检索压力集中到 8 个 FA 层）已被多篇独立论文从实验和理论两个方向证实，这是本报告分析的基础。

---

### 一、关键理论背景

**"Some Attention is All You Need for Retrieval"** (arXiv:2510.19861, Oct 2025)

这篇论文是你的理论的直接实证支撑。作者在三个 hybrid SSM-Transformer 模型上（RecurrentGemma-2B/9B、Jamba-Mini-1.6）系统性地用 entropy-based top-k sparsification 消融注意力头，同时在 NIAH 上监测检索性能。核心发现：

- **完全消融 FA 层 → 检索能力归零**（SSM 层无任何补偿机制，即使用 JRT prompting 也无法恢复）
- 把 FA 头稀疏到仅剩 15% 依然能维持接近完美的 NIAH 检索，同时保留 84% MMLU 性能
- 结论明确：在 hybrid 模型中，检索能力**专属于** softmax 注意力层，SSM 层不参与

**含义：** 你的 8 个 FA 层可以在头粒度上安全稀疏（同层内保留检索头、丢弃 streaming 头），但跨层消融（把整层从 FA 变成近似算子）会导致检索崩溃。这正是你的 TriangleMix 失败模式。

**"A Provable Expressiveness Hierarchy in Hybrid Linear-Full Attention"** (arXiv:2602.01763, Feb 2026)

理论证明：任意数量的线性注意力层无法替代有限数量 FA 层在 L-sequential function composition（多跳检索）上的能力，差距是指数级的（需要 2^(3L²) 个线性层才能模拟 L 层 FA 的能力）。对 SALA 的直接含义：24 层 GLA 无论如何都不能分担 8 层 FA 的检索负载，所以动 FA 层是"刮骨"而不是"剪枝"。

---

### 二、方法逐一分析

---

#### 1. DuoAttention（MIT，ICLR 2025）
**arXiv: 2410.10819**

**核心机制：** 把同一层内的注意力头分为 Retrieval Heads（保留全长 KV cache）和 Streaming Heads（仅保留常数长度的 sink+window KV），prefill 时 streaming head 使用极稀疏 pattern，retrieval head 保持全注意力。

**是否 training-free：** 严格说不是，但接近——需要用合成 passkey 数据优化每个头的 gate 值（可训练参数仅几千个浮点数，2000 步，8卡几小时）。模型主体权重完全冻结，不需要 fine-tune。

**Hybrid 适用性：** 论文测试了 Llama-2/3、Mistral，**未测试任何 hybrid 模型**。但关键在于它的操作粒度是**头内部**（同一层的不同头），而不是跨层。这正好对应你的场景需求：你不需要动 GLA 层，只需要在 8 个 FA 层内部，把 streaming heads 变成 sink+window 近似，保留 retrieval heads 全注意力。

**NIAH 保留证据：** 在 full attention 基线下 NIAH 100% 保留，1M token 上无退化。

**Prefill 加速：** GQA 模型 prefill 加速最高 1.63×。注意这个数字是在 dense-FA-only 模型上测的；在 SALA 上，8 个 FA 层的 prefill 占比更高（GLA 是 O(N) chunkwise，但 8 层 FA 是 O(N²) 瓶颈），实际加速比取决于 FA 层在 total prefill 时间中的占比。

**为什么在 SALA 上可能奏效而 TriangleMix 失败：** DuoAttention 在头粒度上保留 retrieval heads 的全注意力，只稀疏 streaming heads。TriangleMix 把整层 FA 替换为 sink+window，等于把该层的所有头（包括 retrieval heads）全部截断——这是本质差异。在只有 8 个 FA 层的 SALA 上，每层都可能有不可替代的 retrieval heads。

**落地复杂度：** 需要为 SALA 运行 gate 优化（头分类），代码在 `mit-han-lab/duo-attention`，支持 GQA。你的 SALA 是 nkv=2 极端 GQA，需要验证 streaming head 识别率是否有意义（32 个 Q heads 共享 2 个 KV，头粒度 KV 稀疏的实际效果需要测量）。

---

#### 2. MInference 1.0（Microsoft，NeurIPS 2024 Spotlight）
**arXiv: 2407.02490**

**核心机制：** 离线识别每个注意力头的稀疏模式（A-shape / Vertical-Slash / Block-Sparse），推理时动态构建稀疏索引，用定制 GPU kernel 跳过不重要的 QK 计算块。

**是否 training-free：** 是。模式识别是离线 profiling，推理时无额外参数。

**Hybrid 适用性：** 测试模型：LLaMA-3-8B-262K、GLM-4-9B-1M、Yi-9B-200K、Phi-3、Qwen2。**无任何 hybrid 模型测试**。论文中明确提到与 GQA 不兼容的问题（一些稀疏方法需要 per-head 独立 KV，GQA 共享 KV 会干扰稀疏索引），但 MInference 自称已适配 GQA。

**NIAH 保留证据：** 在全 FA 模型上 NIAH 100%（PassKey retrieval = 100.0）。未测 hybrid。

**Prefill 加速：** 在 A100 上 1M token prefill 最高 10×；实际长上下文场景（100K-256K）大约 3-5×。

**为什么在 SALA 可能奏效：** MInference 的稀疏模式（尤其是 Vertical-Slash）对应"少数关键 token 被大量头强关注"，这恰好是 retrieval heads 的特征。在 SALA 的 8 个 FA 层上跑 MInference，等于针对每个头的**实际**注意力模式定制稀疏策略，而不是强加 sink+window 这种通用假设。**关键假设：** SALA 的 FA 层头应该也会呈现 A-shape/Vertical-Slash 模式（这是 long-context Transformer 的通用现象），但需要实测 profiling 验证。如果模式显著（通常如此），MInference 会自动把检索关键 token 保留在稀疏集合里。

**风险：** 在只有 8 个 FA 层的情况下，任何一层的稀疏模式一旦被错误分类，NIAH 就可能崩溃（你的 TriangleMix 实验已证明这一点）。MInference 的保险机制是"不压缩 Vertical-Slash 的重要 token"——理论上应该保留 needle，但在 hybrid 模型上未被验证。

**落地复杂度：** 代码成熟（`microsoft/MInference`），支持 SGLang，FP4 兼容性需要测试（依赖 Triton kernel，与 NVFP4 dequant 路径的交互需要验证）。

---

#### 3. FlexPrefill（ByteDance，ICLR 2025 Oral）
**arXiv: 2502.20766**

**核心机制：** MInference 的改进版。用 Jensen-Shannon divergence 在线判断每个头应该用 query-specific 稀疏模式还是预定义模式，再用 cumulative attention sum 阈值动态决定计算多少 token（而非固定 budget）。

**是否 training-free：** 是。完全在线，无离线 profiling 开销。

**Hybrid 适用性：** 测试：LLaMA-3.1-8B-128K、GLM-4-9B-1M、Yi-9B-200K、Qwen2-7B-128K。**无 hybrid 测试。**

**NIAH/RULER 保留：** RULER 上平均 89.18（vs 全注意力 88.70），超过 MInference 的 85.42。这个数字说明 FlexPrefill 的动态 budget 比固定稀疏更能保留检索能力。

**Prefill 加速：** 论文展示 latency-accuracy Pareto 明显优于 MInference；绝对加速数字以图表形式呈现，约 2-4× 在 full-FA 模型上。

**对 SALA 的分析：** FlexPrefill 比 MInference 更适合 SALA 的原因：它的 cumulative attention threshold 机制意味着，当某个 FA 层的某个头有强烈的 retrieval spike（needle token 的 attention score 极高），该 token 会自动被保留到稀疏集合中。这种 query-aware 自适应比 MInference 的离线模式分配更鲁棒。但同样未在 hybrid 上验证。

---

#### 4. SpargeAttention（Tsinghua，ICML 2025）
**arXiv: 2502.18137**

**核心机制：** 真正 universal 的 training-free 稀疏注意力。两阶段在线过滤：Stage 1 用压缩 Q/K（mean pooling）预测哪些 QK block 不重要；Stage 2 在 online softmax 过程中利用 max logit 值直接跳过 negligible 块（zero additional overhead）。

**是否 training-free：** 是，完全 in-kernel，无离线 profiling，无参数。

**Hybrid 适用性：** 论文称 "accelerates any model inference"，测试了文本（Llama 3.1-8B）、视频生成（CogVideoX）、图像生成（Flux/SD3.5）。**未测 hybrid 语言模型**，但声称对任意 attention 层适用。

**NIAH 保留：** Llama 3.1-8B 128K NIAH：SpargeAttn 0.909 vs 全注意力 0.907（轻微提升，因为稀疏引入了正则化效果）。

**Prefill 加速：** Llama 3.1-8B 128K：端到端从 52s 降至 30s（≈1.7×）。纯注意力层加速 708.1 TOPS，更高。

**为什么对 SALA 最有吸引力：** SpargeAttn 的机制不依赖任何关于"有多少注意力层"的假设——它在每个 attention forward call 中独立决策，根据当前 Q/K 的实际内容动态判断哪些块可跳过。这意味着在 SALA 的 8 个 FA 层上，如果某个块包含 needle token（attention score 高），Stage 2 的 softmax-aware filter 会自动保留它。**这种动态 content-aware 机制从理论上应该比任何基于模式假设的方法更适合 hybrid 场景。** 代码在 `thu-ml/SpargeAttn`，已是 ICML 2025 接收成果。

---

#### 5. Star Attention（NVIDIA，2024）
**arXiv: 2411.17116**

**核心机制：** 分布式 prefill——把上下文切成块分散到多个 GPU，每个 GPU 处理自己的块 + anchor block（首段），query 处理时全局做注意力。消除序列并行中的全局通信开销。

**是否 training-free：** 是，无需 fine-tune。

**Hybrid 适用性：** 测试了 Llama 和 Mamba 模型，但**未在 GLA/Lightning Attention hybrid 上测试**。理论上 GLA 层也可以 block-parallel（chunkwise GLA 已经支持），但 cross-block state propagation 的语义是否等价需要验证。

**NIAH 保留：** single-NIAH 与全注意力基本相同（97-100%）；multi-NIAH 和 multi-hop 有明显退化（信息需要跨 GPU 传播，而 block-local 计算截断了这种通路）。

**对 SALA 的分析：** Star Attention 解决的是**多 GPU 分布**问题，不是单卡稀疏加速。如果你在单张 RTX 6000D 上运行，它不直接适用。且 multi-NIAH 退化问题在 SALA 这种高检索压力架构上会被放大。暂不推荐。

---

#### 6. BLASST（2025）
**arXiv: 2512.12087**

**核心机制：** 复用 FlashAttention 的 online softmax 统计来识别 negligible attention block，用固定 scalar threshold（与 context length 成反比）跳过计算。支持 MHA/GQA/MQA/MLA 全部变体。

**是否 training-free：** 是，threshold 离线标定一次即可（对每个模型只需一个 prefill threshold 和一个 decode threshold）。

**Hybrid 适用性：** 测试了 Llama-3.1-8B、Qwen3-8B 以及 DeepSeek-R1（MLA）。**未测 hybrid。** 但由于它在 kernel 层面操作，理论上可以直接插入 SALA 的 FA 层的 FlashInfer backend。

**NIAH 保留：** 在 RULER/LongBench 上降级极小；NIAH 在标准全 FA 模型上保留。未测 hybrid。

**Prefill 加速：** 71.9% 稀疏度下 1.52× prefill 加速。

**落地复杂度：** 与你的 FlashInfer/FlashAttention kernel 集成难度中等；需要验证与 NVFP4 dequant 的兼容性。

---

#### 7. SeerAttention（Microsoft，2024）
**arXiv: 2410.13276**

**核心机制：** 在模型中加入可学习 AttnGate（pool Q/K → 线性层 → 预测 block 稀疏 mask），通过 self-distillation 训练 gate。

**是否 training-free：** **不是**。需要轻量 fine-tune（只训 gate 参数，few-shot self-distillation），但这仍是 retraining。对于"不能动基座模型"的约束，这个方法**不符合要求**，排除。

---

#### 8. SwiftKV（2024）
**arXiv: 2410.03960**

**核心机制：** 用前面层的输出预计算后面层的 KV cache，让 prompt token 跳过模型后半段的计算（每层只需跑一次 attention）。

**是否 training-free：** **不是**。需要 knowledge distillation fine-tune（只微调受影响层的 Q/K/V projection）。排除。

---

#### 9. DuoAttention 头分类 + MInference 模式稀疏的组合路线（你的 SALA 专属建议）

以上分析指向一个最有希望的 training-free 路线：**在 8 个 FA 层内部做头粒度稀疏，而非动任何一整层**。具体而言：

- 用 DuoAttention 的 gate optimization（仅 2000 步合成数据）识别哪些头是 retrieval heads（必须全注意力），哪些是 streaming heads（可以 sink+window）
- 对 streaming heads 应用 MInference 的 Vertical-Slash 或 SpargeAttn 的 online filter
- 对 retrieval heads 保持 InfLLM-v2 的 block-score top-K 稀疏（你已有的方案）——因为即使是 retrieval heads，InfLLM-v2 的 content-aware 稀疏也比全注意力便宜，且已被 SALA 作者证明 NIAH 安全

这个组合不需要 retrain 主模型（DuoAttention 的 gate 步骤虽然需要梯度，但参数量极小且训练目标是 passkey，不影响模型权重）。

---

### 三、"能否加速 FA 层"的学界共识

基于以上研究，学界目前的共识是：

1. **跨层删除或整层近似 FA 层 → 危险**（TriangleMix 就是这个路线）。"Some Attention is All You Need for Retrieval" 的结论非常清楚：hybrid 模型中 SSM/GLA 层无任何检索备份能力，FA 层是孤注一掷的检索基础设施。

2. **同层内头粒度稀疏 → 安全**。同一层内，streaming heads（focus on sink+recent）占大多数，retrieval heads 是少数但关键的部分。只要 retrieval heads 被保留为全注意力（或 content-aware 稀疏），NIAH 不会崩溃。DuoAttention 在 full-FA 模型上验证了这一点；"Some Attention is All You Need" 在 hybrid 模型上验证了"15% heads 足够"。

3. **加速 GLA/Lightning 层才是真正的 free lunch**。GLA 的 chunkwise prefill 已经是 O(N·d²/chunk) 复杂度，chunk size 是可调节的并行效率杠杆。SALA 的 TTFT 主要瓶颈是 8 个 FA 层的 O(N²) 计算；在 256K context 下，即使 1个 FA 层的 prefill flops 也等于约 30 个 GLA 层。所以 GLA 层侧基本没有 training-free 稀疏的空间（已经是线性了），加速只能来自 FA 层的安全稀疏。

4. **没有论文明确提出"FA 层不能碰"**，但所有 hybrid-aware 工作的隐含结论是一致的：FA 层必须以头粒度处理，不能以层粒度删除或近似。

---

### 四、优先级排序（针对你的环境）

| 优先级 | 方法 | 理由 |
|---|---|---|
| **P1** | SpargeAttn (2502.18137) | 完全 training-free，ICML 2025，content-aware online filter 不依赖模式假设，NIAH 保留已验证，Triton/CUDA kernel 可能与 FlashInfer 集成 |
| **P2** | DuoAttention 头分类 → streaming heads 稀疏 (2410.10819) | 最直接对应 "retrieval head 保护" 理论，gate 优化轻量；需要测 SALA nkv=2 GQA 下的头分类质量 |
| **P3** | FlexPrefill (2502.20766) | MInference++ 变体，cumulative threshold 比固定 budget 更适合 needle 保留，RULER 上超过 MInference |
| **P4** | MInference (2407.02490) | 成熟，有 SGLang 集成，但离线模式分类在 hybrid 未验证 |
| **P5** | BLASST (2512.12087) | 最简单 kernel patch，threshold 标定成本低，但加速比相对低（1.5×） |

**不推荐：** Star Attention（multi-NIAH 退化，单卡无益），SeerAttention（需要 fine-tune），SwiftKV（需要 distillation fine-tune），TriangleMix 变体（已被你的实验否定）。

## 三 agent 共识 + 矛盾点

**共识（高置信度）**：

1. **Triangle 失败的根因是 granularity，不是 implementation**：per-layer binary 砍掉整层就等于砍掉那层里所有 retrieval heads；per-head binary 才是对的范式 — DuoAttention / MInference 都是这个思路。

2. **Hybrid 模型上的 retrieval 是 "孤注一掷"**：agent 1 引用了 "Some Attention is All You Need for Retrieval" (arXiv 2510.19861) 和 "Provable Expressiveness Hierarchy" (arXiv 2602.01763) — 这两篇直接证伪了"让 GLA 多担一点 retrieval 来释放 FA 层"的幻想，理论上 linear attention 替代不了 FA 在多跳检索的能力（指数差距）。**FA 层 = retrieval 唯一通道**，这跟你的实验现象 (E_top1 cwe -22%、F_top2 niah cliff) 完全吻合。

3. **InfLLM-v2 baseline 已经在 training-free Pareto 前沿**（agent 2 和 3 都强调）：mean-pooled K + 完整 stage1 FA 是最高质量的 proxy 信号，per-token + per-head-group 是最细的真动态粒度。SeerAttention TF (NIAH 0.72)、MInference (per-head 但所有 Q 共享 K 位置)、FlexPrefill (first-token proxy 粗) 都没有材料上的更优。

| **B. SpargeAttention** (2502.18137, ICML 2025) | online softmax-aware filter，content-aware | 严格 free | Llama 0.909 vs full 0.907 | 中，hybrid 未验证 |

**关键洞察**：64→48 只砍 25% 候选块、每 query 少看 1024 token（相对 128K ctx 不到 1%），但精度直接归零。这强烈暗示 **InfLLM-v2 的 topk=64 是该模型训练时校准过的**（config.json `sparse_config.topk: 64` 就是模型作者写死的训练时设定），不是经验性 tunable 超参 — 跟下面这个比例失配就 OOD。

也就是：**InfLLM-v2 设计成了「训练-推理对齐」的稀疏 budget**，不像 Triangle 那种 training-free pattern。降 topk = 隐式做 OOD inference。

/user_4813494d/openbmb/kernels/infllmv2_cuda_impl/README.md
# InfLLM V2 CUDA Kernel Implementation

This repository contains the optimized CUDA kernel implementation for **InfLLM V2's Two-Stage Sparse Attention Mechanism**. Our implementation provides high-performance kernels for both Stage 1 (Top-K Context Selection) and Stage 2 (Sparse Attention Computation), enabling Large Language Models (LLMs) to efficiently process long contexts with trainable sparse patterns.

## Overview

InfLLM V2 introduces a novel two-stage approach for efficient long-context processing:
- **Stage 1: Top-K Context Selection**: Block scoring and aggregation using semantic kernels (kernel computes and aggregates scores, selection performed externally)
- **Stage 2: Sparse Attention Computation**: Attention calculation on selected blocks

This CUDA kernel implementation includes both stages, providing:
- Optimized relevance score computation and aggregation for Stage 1 (Top-K selection performed externally)
- Efficient sparse attention on selected blocks for Stage 2
- Significant reduction in computational costs for both forward and backward phases


Built upon [FlashAttention](https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention), our kernels leverage efficient memory access patterns and optimized implementations for both stages.

![InfLLM V2 Architecture](assets/infllm-v2.jpg)

## Open Source Resources

*Updated: 2025-12-01*

We have released the training data and base model for InfLLM V2:

🔗 **Training Data**: https://huggingface.co/datasets/openbmb/InfLLM-V2-data-5B  
🔗 **Initial Model**: https://huggingface.co/openbmb/InfLLM-V2-Short-Dense-Base    
🔗 **Final Model**: https://huggingface.co/openbmb/InfLLM-V2-Long-Sparse-Base


The optimized Stage 1 implementation has been integrated into this repository.

## Two-Stage Architecture

### Stage 1: Top-K Context Selection
The Top-K selection stage involves three sequential steps:
1. **Relevance Score Computation**: Computing scores between query tokens and each semantic kernel (compressed representations of key-value blocks), followed by softmax normalization
2. **Score Aggregation**: Aggregating relevance scores for each semantic kernel across the query group dimension using dimension reduction (hdim16_reduce)
3. **Block Selection (Post-processing)**: Selecting the top-K context blocks for each query token based on the aggregated scores

Note: The `infllmv2_attn_stage1` kernel handles steps 1 and 2 (score computation and aggregation). Only step 3 (Top-K selection) is performed outside the kernel.

### Stage 2: Sparse Attention Computation
The sparse attention stage performs standard attention computation, but only on the blocks selected in Stage 1:
- Support for both forward and backward passes
- Efficient memory access through block-sparse patterns

## Kernel Design Features
- **Token-level Query, Block-level Key-Value**: Avoids training-inference inconsistency during decoding
- **Trainable Context Selection**: Semantic kernels updated indirectly through token-level key vector optimization
- **Selective Block Attention**: Performs attention only on blocks selected in Stage 1

## Kernel Implementation Details

### Stage 1 Kernels
- `infllmv2_attn_stage1`: Calculates similarity scores between query tokens and compressed key representations
- Performs score aggregation across query group dimension (hdim16_reduce)
- Returns aggregated attention scores for subsequent Top-K selection (selection performed outside the kernel)
- Support for causal masking and variable sequence lengths

### Stage 2 Kernels
- `infllmv2_sparse_attn_fwd`: Forward pass kernel for sparse attention
- `infllmv2_sparse_attn_bwd`: Backward pass kernel for training

## Installation

### Requirements

- PyTorch 1.12+
- CUDA 11.6+ (with CUDA development toolkit)
- Python 3.7+
- Linux operating system
- Sufficient GPU memory for kernel compilation
- Ninja build system (for faster compilation)

### Build from Source

#### For Training / Inference (main branch)

```bash

# Install with CUDA kernel compilation
pip install -e .

```


## Usage

### CUDA Kernel API

The InfLLM V2 CUDA kernel provides the following interfaces for the two-stage sparse attention:

#### Stage 1: Attention Score Computation and Aggregation (feature_infer branch)

```python
from infllm_v2 import infllmv2_attn_stage1

# Stage 1: Compute and aggregate relevance scores between queries and semantic kernels
```

ABSTRACT
Long-sequence processing is a critical capability for modern large language mod-
els. However, the self-attention mechanism in the standard Transformer architec-
ture faces severe computational and memory bottlenecks when processing long
sequences. While trainable sparse attention methods offer a promising solution,
existing approaches such as NSA introduce excessive extra parameters and dis-
rupt the conventionalpretrain-on-short, finetune-on-longworkflow, resulting in
slow convergence and difficulty in acceleration. To overcome these limitations,
we introduce dense-sparse switchable attention framework, termed as InfLLM-
V2. InfLLM-V2 is a trainable sparse attention that seamlessly adapts models from
short to long sequences. Specifically, InfLLM-V2 reuses dense attention param-
eters through parameter-free architecture modification, maintaining consistency
between short and long sequence processing. Additionally, InfLLM-V2 ensures
computational efficiency across all sequence lengths, by using dense attention for
short inputs and smoothly transitioning to sparse attention for long sequences. To
achieve practical acceleration, we further introduce an efficient implementation
of InfLLM-V2 that significantly reduces the computational overhead. Our ex-
periments on long-context understanding and chain-of-thought reasoning demon-
strate that InfLLM-V2 is 4×faster than dense attention while retaining 98.1% and
99.7% of the performance, respectively. Based on the InfLLM-V2 framework, we
have trained and open-sourced MiniCPM4.11, a hybrid reasoning model, provid-
ing a reproducibl

Given the limitations of training-free attention mechanisms, trainable sparse attention mechanisms
have garnered increasing attention from researchers (Lu et al., 2025; Gao et al., 2024). Among
them, the natively trainable sparse attention (NSA) (Yuan et al., 2025) method adopts the widely-
used block-sparse attention (Child et al., 2019) structure, designing three different sparse attention
modules and developing corresponding CUDA kernels to accelerate model computation. Despite
its effectiveness, we findmisalignment between the sparse architecture of NSA and the stan-
dard pretrain-on-short, finetune-on-long workflow. A widely used way to build long LLMs is
to pretrain on short sequences and finetune on long sequences. The NSA creates an architectural
mismatch with vanilla full attention, as it introduces three sets of key-value parameters and three
attention modules, forcing the model to abruptly switch from a single-output attention to a multi-
output attention architecture. As shown in Section 4, this mismatch destabilizes training, erases what
the model has already learned, and introduces a significant efficiency bottleneck for short sequences.
To address all the above issues, we propose dense-sparse switchable attention framework (InfLLM-
V2). InfLLM-V2 is built on InfLLM (Xiao et al., 2024a), a training-free block-sparse attention
mechanism, and introduces three core innovations:
1.Seamless Short-to-Long Adaptation:As depicted in Figure 1, different from NSA, which re-
quires additional parameters and multiple attention modules, InfLLM-V2 seamlessly transitions
from dense to sparse attention by directly reusing existing dense attention parame

Preprint. Under review
tation (Xiao et al., 2024b; Han et al., 2024; Child et al., 2019; Zaheer et al., 2020; Beltagy et al.,
2020; Xiao et al., 2025). For instance, sliding window attention restricts each token to interact only
with neighboring tokens (Beltagy et al., 2020). Building upon sliding windows, some works select
special tokens such as initial tokens or segment separators, requiring all tokens to attend to these
special tokens (Xiao et al., 2024b; Chen et al., 2024; Child et al., 2019). These approaches typically
rely on human observations to formulate heuristic rules for selecting relevant contexts.
Dynamic Sparse Patterns.Dynamic sparse patterns incorporate the semantic information of
query tokens into the context selection process by computing the relevance between query tokens
and candidate contexts. Early works primarily perform similarity computation at the token level (Ki-
taev et al., 2020; Roy et al., 2021; Wang et al., 2020). As sequence lengths increase, block sparse
methods have gained widespread adoption, which partition contexts into contiguous block units and
perform relevance computation and context selection at the block granularity (Xiao et al., 2024a;
Jiang et al., 2024; Xu et al., 2025; Tang et al., 2024; Zhang et al., 2025b; Lai et al., 2025). Further-
more, research on attention sparsity has inspired the development of key-value (KV) eviction and
compression methods, which reduce memory consumption by discarding or compressing KV caches
with low attention probabilities (Zhang et al., 2023; Li et al., 2024; Huang et al., 2024; 2025).
Training-free methods, while focusing on improving the inference efficiency of dense attention mod-
els, are often constrained by insufficient sparsity levels in order to avoid severe performance degra-
dation and finally suffer from limited acceleration benefits.
